doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Jazz radio stations never play his music
summary: Stations play little real jazz and turn young people away.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: It’s like how can you duplicate Trane? How can you duplicate Bird or Sweets or Prez or Diz? You know it’s just like these so-called radio stations. They call themselves jazz stations. Now I purposely don’t listen to them, but I listened to them all last week, right? Because I was home. And the whole length of time I was listening to them, the whole week, I think they played one Charlie Parker record, and one Dizzy Gillespie record. A whole week. Never Chico Hamilton.
Yeah, I was going to say, did you get in there. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Never. They don’t play my music. Maybe they’ve got something against me. I was a bad guy or something, I talked about them or something. Who cares. But they do a lot to dictate what people will listen to, and they also turn a lot of people off, especially a lot of young people won’t listen to jazz, because they don’t want to hear what these people really think jazz is. That’s something to think about, right?
Yeah. Somehow we’ve managed to make jazz —
Hard to like. You know you have to go to a lot of work to —
